expectations.text: The reply opens with the recommendation and does not put the whole product and engineering organisation on the rebrand: it protects capacity for the top customer problems.
expectations.evidence: 'Plan Q1 around the three customer problems first, and shrink the rebrand to its must-have core (name, legal entity, domain with redirects) so it doesn't take the capacity that slow invoicing, the broken accounting integration and missing reports need.'

expectations.text: The reply splits the rebrand into a small must-have part (for example the name in the app, domain redirects, legal text) and parts that can wait or be phased (for example a full design system), and makes the cost of each visible.
expectations.evidence: 'Must-have rebrand, small: the new name in the app, legal and billing entities, domain with redirects and email'; 'Phased, not dropped: the full design system and the new marketing site'. Cost: 'Ask the teams to estimate the rebrand pieces and the three fixes themselves' and 'Rebrand scope with dates'.

expectations.text: The reply ranks the customer problems with evidence (for example NPS comments, churn or revenue at risk, support tickets) and sets measures for fixing them.
expectations.evidence: Lists evidence ('NPS comments, churn reasons, support tickets and the ARR of accounts tied to the invoicing, integration and reports complaints') and per-fix measures ('invoice time, integration error rate, report usage, detractor share'). But the evidence is rolled up into one figure ('X% of detractors cite these three issues, Y of ARR is at risk') and the three problems are never ranked against each other.

expectations.text: The reply brings leadership options with explicit trade-offs instead of a flat no.
expectations.evidence: 'offer two or three options, such as full rebrand in Q1, core rebrand plus customer fixes, or customer fixes first with a rebrand date in Q2. Say which you recommend and why'. The trade-off is explicit in the question 'what NPS and renewal risk are we willing to accept for the rest?', though the trade-offs per option are thin.

expectations.text: The reply handles "leadership decides, teams execute" and "any decision beats no decision" constructively: a private conversation first, asking for the reasons, separating decisions that are cheap to reverse from ones that aren't, and offering a light decision process, without labelling or attacking the leaders.
expectations.evidence: 'With the CEO, in private first. Ask for a 30-minute conversation before any wider forum'; asks 'Which parts of the rebrand are truly Q1-critical' and which dates are fixed versus 'only feel urgent'; '"Any decision beats no decision" holds for choices that are cheap to undo... Pushing the whole organisation into one quarter of rebrand work is hard to undo'; 'Ask for a one-page decision record with the problem, options, reasons, and a review date'; 'Let leaders save face'.

expectations.text: The reply is practical and short enough to act on (roughly 500 words or less), with any longer plan offered or attached as a separate document.
expectations.evidence: 593 words (wc -w), above the 550 ceiling, and no separate document was attached.

factual_errors.evidence: 'NPS has fallen 24 points' is correct. No wrong claims found.

skill_leak.evidence: No mention of skills, reference files or internal jargon.

owns_result.evidence: No leader says the responsibility for the NPS fall or the open complaints is leadership's.

best_insight.value: It keeps the customer-fix teams out of the rebrand entirely, and it has teams estimate both workloads from their own past throughput rather than setting the split from the top.

suggestions.assertion: The reply ranks the customer problems with evidence (for example NPS comments, churn or revenue at risk, support tickets) and sets measures for fixing them.
suggestions.reason: 'Ranks' is ambiguous. Most replies ask for evidence on the three complaints together and set measures, but few put them in order. I passed a sample only when it broke the evidence down per complaint (ARR, tickets or detractor comments per issue) or gave an explicit order. Consider rewording to 'sizes each complaint with its own evidence and puts them in order'.

No assertion checks the technical link between the new domain and the broken accounting integration (OAuth redirect URIs, webhooks, sending-domain reputation, customer allowlists). Most samples raised it, and it is the most practical sequencing argument. Capacity realism (no overtime, slack for incidents) and committing to the decision once it is made also go unchecked.

eval_feedback.overall: Good structure and good handling of the CEO, but slightly over length, and the customer evidence is aggregated rather than used to rank the three problems.
